article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: A wet kickoff in London, Jalen Hurts to injured reserve, and overnight line movement with the Bills.

items.headline: Sunday starts at Wembley at 9:30 a.m. ET
paragraphs: The first kickoff of the day is in London. The Texans face the Jaguars at Wembley at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network, the last of three straight London games.
Jacksonville is -2.5 with a 42.5 total on DraftKings, unchanged from Saturday. The Jaguars are 4-1; the Texans are 1-4 but finally won last week.
It's a wet London morning: rain is likely right around the 2:30 p.m. local kickoff with a chance of lingering showers, about 57 degrees and a 10-12 mph breeze. The field could be slick.
If you're playing anything in this game, plan it now. London inactives post about 90 minutes before kickoff, roughly 8:00 a.m. ET.
items.takeaway: London goes first, so plan it first: check the app's card and inactives before 9:30 a.m. ET.

items.headline: Quarterback roundup: Hurts to IR, Williams and Penix are go
paragraphs: The biggest news of the morning: Philadelphia placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve Saturday with the blood clot in his left calf. He has to miss at least four games, so Tanner McKee starts today against Carolina and, per Ian Rapoport, for the foreseeable future. Saquon Barkley is out again too.
Good news in Atlanta: Caleb Williams is expected to play for the Bears, and Michael Penix Jr. has no injury designation and is expected to start for the Falcons. That game kicks off at 1:00 p.m. ET.
A.J. Brown is back for the Patriots' home game against the Jets.
The app's QB column already has all of this: McKee, Williams, Penix, Winston (in for the Giants), and Huntley starting for Baltimore. Nothing here conflicts with what the app shows.
items.takeaway: Hurts-to-IR makes Philadelphia's QB settled, not week-to-week; Williams and Penix resolved the one real game-day question.

items.headline: Sunday weather: only Wembley is wet
paragraphs: Every U.S. stadium is clear and mild at kickoff. Philly 57, MetLife 58, Cleveland 61, Foxborough 52 — all sunny with almost no wind. Tampa is the warmest at 78 with a 15 mph breeze, the strongest wind on the board.
The late games are clean too: clear 57 at Arrowhead for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, and a clear evening at Lambeau for Sunday night.
This is weather as weather, not an edge: it just means no kickoff window has a forecast worth worrying about outside London.
items.takeaway: File Sunday's weather as clear and mild everywhere but Wembley — it doesn't move any number.

items.headline: Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff
paragraphs: The morning brief can't give you inactives — they don't exist yet. London's list posts around 8:00 a.m. ET, and the 1:00 p.m. ET games post theirs around 11:30 a.m. ET.
If a surprise name shows up on either list, run it back through the app: the board refreshes every morning and evening, and Check will re-evaluate the play on your book's price.
items.takeaway: Check the inactive lists when they post, and let the app re-run the math if something changes.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Today's three cards, with real numbers
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the Bills moneyline at -245 on FanDuel. The app gives Buffalo about 70% to beat the Raiders — this card forgoes value for win probability. Note it's minus-EV at that price, which is the whole point of the card: the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
Balanced is the Packers moneyline at -115 on DraftKings, tonight's Sunday night game against Dallas. The middle ground: the model has Green Bay around 59%, a solid pick without paying Bills prices.
Value is the model's plus-EV play: the Raiders plus 5.5 at -110 on DraftKings. About 54% to cover against a 52% breakeven — small edge, but an edge.
Three cards, three jobs: most likely to win, the reasonable middle, and the model's plus-EV play. Pick the job you actually want done.
items.takeaway: Match the card to your goal today — win chance, balance, or the plus-EV number.

items.headline: Your book's number isn't the card's number? Tap Check
paragraphs: The Bills are -245 at FanDuel and -258 at DraftKings right now. Same team, different price, different verdict — that's exactly why the card shows its book.

If your book has -240, or -260, or a totally different number, don't guess. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
Full re-evaluation, not a blind override: Check tells you whether your number is still playable.
items.takeaway: Never bet the card's price blind — Check your book's price and take the verdict on your number.

items.headline: Learn the Game: tickets vs handle
paragraphs: This morning's free betting-splits board showed no NFL game with a real public-vs-sharp split, so there's no honest Fade today. Instead, here's the vocabulary for reading one when it shows up.

Say a sportsbook reports 70% of tickets on the favorite but only 40% of the handle. Hypothetical numbers, to be clear. Tickets count bets; handle counts dollars. So most bettors are on the favorite, but the money is on the underdog.

That pattern suggests a few big, price-sensitive bets are taking the dog while lots of small bets pile on the favorite. It doesn't prove anything by itself. It becomes interesting when the line also moves toward the dog — the market drifting toward the side the money took.
When you see that combo on a real board, the move is patience: let the public keep pushing the favorite's price, and see if the dog's number gets better without any new bad news about the team.
items.takeaway: Tickets count bets, handle counts dollars — when they disagree and the line drifts toward the money side, wait for a better number instead of chasing.

items.headline: Overnight: Bills moneyline keeps climbing, cards rotate
paragraphs: The Bills moneyline moved from -230 to -245 at FanDuel (-258 at DraftKings) with no new news — that's Sunday money arriving, and the app's Hit Rate card is current on it.
Two cards rotated since Saturday: Balanced moved from the Giants moneyline to the Packers moneyline at -115, and Value moved from Falcons +1.5 to Raiders +5.5 at -110.

Everything else held: Ravens -3.0, Panthers -3.0, Jaguars -2.5 with the 42.5 total in London. The Bears-Falcons line settled at Bears -1.5 once both quarterbacks were confirmed playing, after swinging out to Bears -3 midweek.
If your book is still hanging an older number on any of these, that's exactly what Check is for: type in your book's price and get the verdict.
items.takeaway: Overnight did the moving this time: Bills -230 to -245, two cards rotated, and the app caught all of it.

items.headline: Game-day order of operations
paragraphs: London first: inactives around 8:00 a.m. ET, kickoff 9:30. Then the 1:00 p.m. ET inactives around 11:30 a.m. — skim the list, and if a surprise name shows up, re-run the game through Check.

One timing note for the day: the Bills' price has already drifted from -230 to -245. If your book still shows the old number and Check says bet, bet now — the Sunday rush usually pushes prices the wrong way, not your way.
And the regular nudge: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: London at 9:30, inactives at 11:30, and don't let a good number drift past you while you wait.

evidence.fact: The Eagles placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve Saturday with the superficial blood clot in his left calf; he must miss at least four games (earliest eligibility vs Pittsburgh, Nov 22). Tanner McKee starts Sunday vs Carolina 'and moving forward' (Rapoport/Schefter). Philadelphia also signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster; Saquon Barkley (hamstring) out again.

evidence.fact: Caleb Williams (questionable on the final injury report) is expected to play Sunday at Atlanta, per Rapoport and Schefter. Michael Penix Jr. carries no injury designation and is expected to start for Atlanta (Schefter, Oct 16). The line settled at Bears -1.5 on DraftKings after swinging from Falcons -1.5 out to Bears -3 while Penix's status was in question.
evidence.interpretation: The game's biggest question resolved; both QBs are go.
evidence.app_guidance: The app lists both Williams and Penix as expected starters; inactives (~11:30 a.m. ET) are the final confirmation.
